newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico left accuse PRI of circulating smear video.
newsitem.headline: Mexico left accuse PRI of circulating smear video.

text.p: Leftists accused Mexico's ruling party on Wednesday of organising a smear video to wreck the reputation of the leftist candidate for mayor of Mexico City, who is currently leading in the polls.
In the video, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters, left-wing mayor candidate Cuauhtemoc Cardenas is seen promising a peaceful campaign and a rejection of violence.
His words are cut with images of demonstrators burning buses, hurling Molotov cocktails, spray-painting graffiti and stoning police.
Prominent in some of the rioting are protesters waving banners supporting Cardenas's Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD).
In another scene, Cardenas is seen standing on a platform with a peasant leader who pledges that "the fight will go on, there will be more invasions of land."
As a bell tolls, the words flash up on the screen: "Cardenas never tells you the truth ... They destroy. They don't build. Think before you vote."
The video is signed by two unknown groups: "Business Action" and "National Council of Popular Organisations".

Mexico City residents told radio reporters they had found copies of the five-minute video cassette in their mailboxes. One tire dealer in the capital's Tacubaya district was reported to have handed out copies to clients.
Asked about the video at a campaign stop, Cardenas said: "What you are seeing are desperate measures in the face of what could be a very decisive election result."
Polls put Cardenas way ahead of his nearest challenger -- Alfredo del Mazo of the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) -- in the Mexico City mayor's race.
A victory for the veteran left-winger in the country's biggest city would carry huge symbolic weight and set Cardenas up for a presidential challenge in 2000, analysts say.
Marcos Rascon, a PRD deputy, told Reuters the video "comes from the circles of power ... it comes from the campaign committee of Alfredo del Mazo".
Antonio Garfias, del Mazo's campaign coordinator, strongly denied the video came from the PRI.
"Of course we have nothing to do with it," he told Reuters. "However, I think what hurts the PRD most is that it shows them as they are ... it's very well made".
"That's what Cardenas is like. With his new image and his little smile, people think he's different -- but he's not."

The conservative National Action Party (PAN) also issued a statement on Wednesday accusing the PRI of being behind smear leaflets which falsely accused the PAN of wanting to eliminate free school textbooks and privatise education.
The PRI has ruled Mexico for the last 68 years.
